scoring_justification: The agent's regression fits are the final analysis result; recompute from raw DFT energies is infeasible given the output contract. Structural checks (ordering, sign, intercept magnitude) and reference match for classification provide reliable verification.

outputs.description: Slopes and intercepts from coverage-dependent linear regressions of total adsorption energies. The checker will verify relative ordering (Ag < Au < Pb for HCOO:COOH slope) and that at least two intercepts have magnitude > 0.05 eV.

Selectivity classification of each metal derived from the regression slopes. The checker will compare predicted categories against hidden experimental selectivity (Ag: CO_single, Au: CO_single, Pb: HCOOH).

output_contract.notes: The DFT calculations are computationally intensive; the solving agent may need external compute resources (GPUs, multiple cores). The classification threshold (1.65) and product naming (CO_single/CO_multi) follow the paper's scheme. Regression ordering and intercept magnitude are scored via structural audit; classification accuracy is scored via reference match.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Table 1 and experimental selectivity from Hori et al. 1994 (ref 24) and Hara et al. 1995 (ref 73) as cited in the paper
hidden_assets.generation_method: direct lookup of expected selectivity (CO for Ag, Au; HCOOH for Pb)
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These categories are the experimental consensus reported in the paper itself.

steps.description: Check ordering: Au slope < Ag slope < Pb slope for HCOO_vs_COOH pair
Check that at least two metals have |intercept| > 0.05 eV for HCOO_vs_COOH pair
Check that all three COOH_vs_H slopes are negative
Check predicted categories match experimental selectivity (Ag:CO_single, Au:CO_single, Pb:HCOOH)
